text:
sophia: Hey team — hitting intermittent OOMs on canary when we ramp qps to ~4k. Only seen on the kvcache-heavy route (prefix-lookup path). Heap growth looks linear for ~30s then sudden OOM. Not a full leak across runs but reproducible within the canary namespace.

kevin: Can you paste the root log and a heapshot? also which allocator build (jemalloc/custom)?

sophia: running jemalloc build (release, tcmalloc turned off). here's the last tail of the process log: 

```
I0321 14:12:07.123  pid=1024 kv_cache.cpp:312] prefix_lookup batch=64 tokens=128
I0321 14:12:07.143  pid=1024 kv_cache.cpp:412] kvprefetch: hit_ratio=0.78 active=243MB cache_rss=510MB
I0321 14:12:37.200  pid=1024 oom-reaper: process killed due to allocation failure (alloc 1.2GB)
```

kevin: thx. can you run a heapshot with MALLOC_CONF=lg_chunk:22,prof:true and attach jeprof output? also try `jemalloc_stats` dump.

priya: quick thought — we saw similar spikes when prefix cache eviction and slab reservation interacted in the old allocator. Could be fragmentation from mixed-size slabs. Try forcing smallalloc backpressure in the runtime config: `--smallalloc-max=512k` and see if it delays the OOM.

simon: if you can, run a micro-bench reproducer that streams many small keys to exercise prefix cache. here's the curl loop i use: 

```
for i in $(seq 1 10000); do
  curl -sS "https://canary.api/redwood/prefix?key=k-$((i%1000))" >/dev/null
done
```

ops-bot: Deploy 1867d7 to canary completed at 2024-03-21T14:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

sophia: ran the micro-bench + heapshot. attaching summary: 
- peak_rss before ramp: 520MB
- steady_rss at QPS 3.5k: ~880MB
- growth over 30s: +420MB
- jemalloc prof shows hot allocations in `kv_entry::reserve` and `slab_allocator::alloc_small`

kevin: that points to small-size slab churn. Can you grab `jeprof --svg` and post link. Also try `mallctl` stats: `stats.allocated`, `stats.active`, `stats.metadata` to see fragmented metadata growth.

sophia: posted gist with jeprof svg and mallctl dumps: https://gist.github.com/sophia/abc123 (private)

priya: another experiment — enable prefix KV compaction (runtime flag `--kv-compact=on`) on a single canary pod and re-run. If compaction holds working set smaller, fragmentation drops.

simon: +1 on compaction. also try flipping `--slab-shrink-threshold=0.5` so we release cold slabs sooner. might increase tail latency but good for bisecting the leak vs fragmentation.

kevin: ordering of experiments: 1) smallalloc cap, 2) compaction, 3) slab shrink aggressive. Measure rss slope for 60s each. If none help, we'll capture full core on next run and run heap analyzer.

sophia: starting tests now, will update with short results in ~10m. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:

kevin: ping me after the first run, i'll queue a hotfix branch to tweak slab params if we get signal.

sophia: quick followup — smallalloc cap reduced the slope dramatically, OOM didn't occur in 2 runs. compaction also reduced steady_rss by ~120MB. posting numbers in the gist.

priya: sounds like fragmentation + working set spikes. we should add a canary config that enables compact+smallalloc cap for 24h and monitor. also file a follow-up RFC to consider slab resizing heuristics.

kevin: agreed. let's also add a quick regression test into the allocator perf suite: simulated kvcache workload with varied key sizes. i'll draft it.

sophia: created ticket INF-4122 and added the gist links. thanks all.

simon: nice work. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: Incident monitor: memory-oom-rate for canary route decreased to 0 in last 10m after config change.
